title: Bubble Sort
statement: Given an integer array nums, sort it in ascending order using the Bubble Sort algorithm.
think: What is the task asking? Sort the array using a specific algorithm: bubble sort.
What is the key operation? Compare adjacent elements and swap them if they are in the wrong order.
What wording signals stand out? Sort, bubble, adjacent swaps.
What is the brute force idea? Bubble sort itself is already a simple brute-force sorting algorithm.
What is the better/optimal idea? For learning, implement bubble sort correctly.
What are the edge cases? Already sorted array, duplicates, negative numbers.
What is the complexity? O(n²) time and O(1) extra space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I repeatedly sweep through the array, swapping adjacent out-of-order elements, so the largest unsorted value moves to the end.
algorithm: Loop outer pass from 0 to n - 2
Loop inner index from 0 to n - 2 - pass
After all passes, array is sorted
interview: I would implement bubble sort by repeatedly comparing adjacent elements and swapping them when needed. After each pass, the largest remaining value bubbles to the end.
ru: На каждом проходе мы сравниваем соседние элементы и более большой как будто всплывает вправо.

critical: Stop after one pass and think the array is sorted

gaps: Nice to have: explain why bubble sort is educational but not optimal
whyThisPattern: The task explicitly asks for sorting and names the algorithm, so the pattern is sorting.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Two Pointers, because this is repeated adjacent comparison over multiple passes.
Not HashSet, because uniqueness is not the goal.
